## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Rāhula Sutta* (Snp 2.11; PTS Snp 58) is a discourse in the *Suttanipāta* in which Rāhula reflects upon the spiritual instructions given to him by the Buddha, his father [SuttaCentral]. In an analysis of the ballad forms of the collection, S. M. Katre identifies the opening stanzas (Sn 335–336) as an atypical form of *vatthugāthā* (introductory dialogue verses) consisting of question and answer between interlocutors left unspecified until the closing prose, followed by six stanzas imparting general spiritual admonition [Katre 1931]. The text is attested in nineteenth-century British Library manuscript collections alongside Burmese bilingual paraphrases (*nissaya*) [Bendall 1893].
SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels in non-Pali Āgama or Sanskrit corpora [SuttaCentral]. However, computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 27 matching passages across six Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The concluding sequence of the sutta (§6.4–8.4) is shared directly with two other canonical Pali verse texts: the *Vaṅgīsattheragāthā* (Thag 21.1, §16.2–18.4) and the *Vaṅgīsa Saṃyutta* (SN 8, §4.3.2–4.6.4) [DharmaNexus]. Extensive reuse also occurs in the commentarial literature, notably within the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as the modern *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records a low-scoring machine alignment between segment §3.3 and the Tibetan translation of the *Pratyutpannabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthitasamādhi-sūtra* (D0133), though this is not recognized as a curated parallel [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
